source.title: JI2S: Joint Influence-Aware Instruction Data Selection for Efficient Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Jingyu Wei; Bo Liu; Tian-Jiao Wan; Baoyun Peng; Xing-Kong Ma; Mengmeng Guo

record.file_problem: Text contains the full paper, including appendices; no obvious truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports instruction-data selection and fine-tuning outcomes, not whether networks that fit arbitrary labels generalize, nor any of the mapped conditions or measures in V1–V8. Its results are adjacent to the broad topic of generalization but do not test those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports model benchmark scores for selected training subsets and changes in performance with the joint-influence weight and subset size. These outcomes concern instruction-data selection and downstream capability, not the claim versions. Figure 1's toy experiment is described as sample-level influence on test accuracy, but its reported numerical outcomes are not present in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates instruction-data selection using downstream benchmark performance. It does not test any V1–V8 manipulation or relationship. In particular, influence on held-out loss is not the self-label memorization measure in V8, and neither the main experiments nor the BERT toy experiment compares removing highly memorized examples with removing equally many random examples.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but abbreviated. The authors conclude that selecting 1,000 Alpaca examples using marginal and joint influence generally improves performance over full-data training and strong selection baselines. They argue that moderate, model-dependent joint-influence weighting improves selection and that the selected subset preserves semantic diversity. Their conclusion says improvements hold in most cases; JI²S does not beat every baseline on every benchmark.
record.recipe_differences: Instruction-data selection and instruction fine-tuning, rather than testing arbitrary-label fitting or the mapped generalization conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported benchmark performance varies with the joint-influence weight λ, training subset size, and model. Mistral-7B declines as λ increases; LLaMA2-13B is described as relatively stable.

fits_no_version.finding: JI²S-selected 1,000-example subsets outperform full Alpaca training on average Open LLM benchmark scores for all three models: 64.62 versus 63.34, 72.52 versus 67.70, and 69.65 versus 67.11. LIMA exceeds JI²S for LLaMA2-13B. Training recipes also differ between full-data and subset conditions (Table 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Influence-based instruction-data selection can improve downstream performance over full-data fine-tuning under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: Joint-influence weighting has model-dependent effects: Mistral-7B peaks at λ=0.05 and deteriorates at larger weights; LLaMA2-13B varies relatively little (Table 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The benefit of incorporating pairwise training-example influence depends on its weight and the model.

fits_no_version.finding: The BERT toy experiment examines nonadditive test-accuracy effects of removing subsets A, B, and their union. The supplied text reports no numerical outcomes and does not select subsets using self-label memorization or provide an equal-size random-removal comparison.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training subsets can interact nonadditively in their effects on held-out accuracy.

record.code_released: GitHub repository mentioned, but no URL is stated in the supplied text.
record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The toy sample-interaction experiment is described in Appendix B.1, but its results are not included in the supplied text. Pairwise win-rate results are shown only in figures without numerical values in the text. The supplied text gives no uncertainty values for the main benchmark table; it says the experiments were averaged over three random seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: reported results do not measure a behavior named by V1–V8.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance comparisons between adaptive optimizers and SGD under specified tuning budgets.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove their penalty.
Controlled dropout comparisons, including training-set size and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing examples selected by self-label memorization and comparing retrained test accuracy with equal-size random removal.

record.verdict_notes: Keeping the record's rows empty is appropriate for V1–V8. Adam, batch size, dropout, and weight decay appear as recipe details rather than controlled tests of their generalization effects. Feldman and Zhang (2020) is cited for leave-one-out influence estimation; the study does not test or operationally use its memorization-removal finding.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width grows beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
